why: Evaluate f(21)=4·21^(−1)=4/21 by rewriting negative exponent as reciprocal then substituting. A confuses substitution arithmetic, B and D invert the fraction showing negative-exponent misapplication.
SPR. Set (x+6)(x−4)=0 and apply zero product property to read zeros −6 and 4 directly from factored form.
Substitute x=−1,0,1 into 32·2^x yielding 16,32,64. A and C show linear patterns revealing confusion between linear and exponential growth; B misapplies exponent rules for x=1.
Interpret s(87)≈23 as approximately 23g remain after 87 years. B confuses 'remain' with 'decayed'; C and D swap the input and output roles of the function notation f(a)=b.

g(x)=x²+55 is in vertex form with vertex (0,55); minimum value is 55. A gives the x-coordinate of the vertex instead of the y-value; C doubles the constant; D misreads the upward parabola as having no minimum.
SPR. Evaluate f(0)=0⁵+9(0)+17=17 by substituting x=0 to find the y-intercept b=17.
Set 2C=C·2^(4r) so 4r=1 giving r=1/4. The doubling condition requires rescaling the exponent; A halves instead of quartering, C and D confuse r with the time or its reciprocal.
Translate area=x(x−15)=76 into x²−15x−76=0, factor as (x−19)(x+4)=0, take positive root x=19. A selects the extraneous negative root's magnitude; C and D arise from factoring or setup errors.
Read the graph value at November 2012 to find approximately 5 active projects. All distractors reflect off-by-one or off-by-two graph-reading errors.
The cubic graph visibly crosses the x-axis at three distinct points so f(x)=0 has three solutions. Distractors test whether students can accurately count all crossings from the graph.

Intercepts at −5 (touch), 0 (cross), 4 (cross) require factors x, (x−4), (x+5)² with positive leading coefficient. A and C use wrong signs for intercepts; B has correct zeros but negative leading coefficient contradicting end behavior.

At t=0 (year 2010), D=5640, so 5640 is the predicted traffic for 2010. B misidentifies the initial year; C and D confuse the initial value with a per-year additive or percent increase, conflating exponential with linear growth.

f(0)=3000 is the population when first observed (x=0). A treats the coefficient as an annual decrease (linear thinking); B confuses the coefficient with the percent rate; C evaluates at x=1 instead of x=0.
A 4% annual increase means the multiplier is 1+0.04=1.04. A confuses '4% of' with '4% more than'; B subtracts instead of adding to 1; D uses the raw integer 4 without converting to a decimal rate.
f(0)=33(1.5)^0=33 so c=33 appears as the coefficient. A yields f(0)=1.5, misidentifying which number is c; C and D yield f(0)=1 since b^0=1, so c does not visibly appear as coefficient or base.

Set 2W·W=162 so W²=81, W=9. B gives the length not width (or divides by 2 instead of taking square root); C gives W² without the final root; D uses the raw area without applying the length-width relationship.
7% monthly growth gives c=1300(1.07)^m. A uses 0.07 as the base (confusing '7% of' with '7% more than'); C uses 7 without decimal conversion; D writes a linear model instead of exponential.
SPR. Set 2·40000=40000·2^(t/790), cancel to get 2^1=2^(t/790), so t/790=1 and t=790 minutes. The exponent denominator directly gives the doubling time.

f(0)=4000(0.75)^0=4000, so 4000 is the initial beetle count in 2012 (A). Choices are verbal context statements (NLF.2). B confuses f(1) with f(0); C/D confuse the initial value with the rate of change.

Ratio h(2)/h(0)=1.54/1.23≈1.252=(1.12)^2, so base≈1.12 per year giving h(x)=1.23(1.12)^x (D). A uses the rate 0.12 as the base; B rescales the exponent unnecessarily; C uses decay base 0.88 instead of growth 1.12.
g(0)=1 and g(1)=1/25, so base=1/25; (1/25)^(-1)=25 ✓ and (1/25)^2=1/625 ✓ giving answer D. A reverses the base-exponent relationship; B and C use partial roots (5 or 1/5) instead of 1/25.
Monthly growth factor 606.42/604=1.004, so n=604(1+0.004)^t (C). A/B use 0.4 instead of 0.004 (forgetting to convert the percent correctly); D divides exponent by 12 when t is already in months.

Vertex form y=-16(x-5.6)²+502 has vertex (5.6,502); since a<0 this is the maximum. The rocket's max height is 502 ft at 5.6 s (B). A swaps the vertex coordinates; C/D confuse the vertex with the launch point.
p(x)=x²-57, an upward parabola with vertex at x=0, so min p(0)=-57 (B). A doubles -57; C gives the min of x² forgetting the constant; D flips the sign.
Length=15w and y=(15w)(w)=area. So 15w is the length (A). B confuses length with width; C and D confuse a factor with the perimeter or the product itself.
Let second=n; first=2n+5. n(2n+5)=462 gives 2n²+5n-462=0. Discriminant=3721=61²; n=56/4=14. First=33. Smaller integer is 14.
f(x)=g(x)(x+3). At x=0: f(0)=g(0)·3=12·3=36, so y-intercept is (0,36) (A). B uses g(0) directly; C reads a different table value; D likely from an algebraic misstep.
h(0)=2(16)-32=0 ✓. Vertex at x=4; by parabola symmetry the other zero is at x=8 since (0+8)/2=4 (D). C uses the axis of symmetry itself as the other zero.
f(x)=x²-48x+2304=(x-24)²+1728. Minimum value is 1728 at x=24.
f(0)=(-8)(2)^0+22=-8+22=14, so y-intercept is (0,14) (A). C takes only the additive constant 22; D takes only the coefficient -8; both ignore the other term.
Set y=0: -100x²+1400x+7200=0 → x²-14x-72=0 → (x-18)(x+4)=0. Roots 18 and -4; max x with y≥0 is 18 (D). B gives the vertex x=7; A/C come from factoring errors.
f(0)=9000(0.66)^0=9000, so the company sent 9000 ads in 1997 (A). B computes f(1)=5940 instead of f(0); C/D misread the base 0.66 as a percent decrease (66% vs 34%).
Geometric sequence: a₁=9, ratio=4, so aₙ=9·4^(n-1) giving w=9(4^(n-1)) (D). A/B swap the first term and ratio; C uses n instead of n-1.

f(0)=a(2.2^0+2.2^b)=a(1+2.2^b). In Form I the constant term a·2.2^b is not the full y-intercept; in Form II the y-intercept is hidden inside the parentheses. Neither displays it as a visible constant or coefficient (D).
Zeros at x=44 and x=46; minimum of upward parabola at the midpoint x=(44+46)/2=45 (B). A/C pick a zero instead of the vertex; D is unrelated.
g(x)=f(x)+6 is a vertical shift (NLF.5); evaluating g(4)=f(4)+6=(3)(7)(2)+6=48 is function evaluation (NLF.1). SPR, no distractor options.
Vertex form h=-16(t-1.8)^2+51.84 from max height 51.84 at t=1.8 (NLF.4). A/C use +1.8 (wrong shift direction), D negates the vertical offset.
Substituting x=0 into f(x)=a^x+b gives 1+b=-323 so b=-324 (NLF.1 unknown constant from y-intercept). SPR.

Choices are verbal context statements (NLF.2). The x-intercept a=50 means revenue=$0 at that price (B). Factor -500x(x-50)=0 for zeros (NLF.4). A confuses zero with vertex, C/D mix up axes/intercepts.
Bacteria double daily (exponential, NLF.3). From Day 3 at 10^6, need 2^9=512 more doublings to reach 5.12x10^8, so Day 12. A treats growth linearly, B/C miscount the starting day.
f(-9)=f(3) gives axis x=-3; equating -2/a=-3 yields a=2/3<1 so II is false. k=c-6<0 allows c in (0,6), so I is not necessarily true. Answer D (NLF.4 quadratic structure).
P(t)=260(1.04)^((6/4)t): exponent advances 1 when (3/2)t=1, so t=2/3 year=8 months (NLF.3 exponent time scaling). B ignores the 6/4 multiplier, C/D multiply instead of divide.
f has vertex at x=-64/8=-8 (NLF.4); g(x)=f(x+5) shifts left 5 (NLF.5), so minimum at x=-8-5=-13. B omits the shift, C uses only the shift, D shifts right.
Read vertex (-1,-8) and y-intercept (0,-6) from graph (NLF.1/CL.0072); c=-6 from x=0, then -b/4=-1 gives b=4 (NLF.4); bc=4x(-6)=-24. SPR.
Parabola vertex at t=3; by symmetry returns to launch height at t=2x3=6 (NLF.4). A stops at the vertex, C confuses 7m height with time, D miscalculates.
Minimum of y=x^2-14x+22 at x=-(-14)/(2x1)=7 (NLF.4 vertex via -b/2a). SPR.
Volume = lwh = 11·x·(x-1) writes a quadratic model from dimensions (NLF.4, AV.3). B/C/D use subtraction or addition instead of multiplication.
f(x)-15 shifts down 15 (NLF.5); at x=0: b-16=-99/7 gives b=13/7; then a=(65/7)/(13/7)=5 (NLF.1 constants from points). SPR.
(24,0) on g means (24+14)(t-24)=0 so t=24 (NLF.4 factored-form zero); then g(0)=(14)(24)=336 (NLF.1 evaluate). SPR.
Length x, width x-24, area x(x-24)=2661 (NLF.4 quadratic model from words). A reverses the subtraction, C/D add instead of multiply.
Zeros at 14 and -19; vertex x=(14+(-19))/2=-5/2 (NLF.4 factored form + symmetry). A computes the product, B picks a zero, C misreads a sign.
f(-4)=3+|8-16|=11, then g(11)=11/10-6=-49/10. Two-step function evaluation (NLF.1). SPR.
Product of x and (x+91) is x(x+91) (NLF.4 quadratic from words). B uses x-91, C/D misinterpret 'product'.
150% more → multiplier 2.50 not 1.50 (percent-more vs factor); 180 at y=1 gives S₀=72 at y=0. Exponential model writing with percent→factor conversion and initial-value solve.
Absolute-value equation |59−2k|=3k splits into two cases; only 59−2k=3k yields valid k=59/5 (Case 2 gives negative, rejected). Function notation substitution plus absolute-value case handling.
g(t)=f(t)+3 shifts max up by 3; f(t)=−2t²+55t has vertex at t=55/4 and max 2(55/4)². Completing the square gives max g = 3+2(55/4)². Transformation plus quadratic vertex.
Population decreases → multiplier (1+r) must be between 0 and 1, so −1<r<0. Recognizing growth vs decay by the sign of r in the exponential model.
Graph shows ab^x+c with horizontal asymptote and no x-axis crossing, so f(x)=0 for zero values of x. Exponential asymptote behavior read from graph.
Exponent x/12 means base 0.64 applies per 12 months (1 year); yearly decrease is 1−0.64=0.36 → p=36. Exponent time-unit rescaling and percent↔factor conversion.
Vertex form (1/9)(x−7)²+3 gives vertex (7,3); positive leading coefficient → minimum. Best interpretation: minimum height is 3 inches. Context interpretation of vertex.
y-intercept at t=0 gives f(0)=8000; t=0 is end of 1998. Best interpretation: 8000 coupons sent at end of 1998. Context interpretation of exponential y-intercept.

f(x)=−6(3)^x−3 approaches −3 from below as x→−∞ and goes to −∞; g(x)=−3(6)^x approaches 0 from below and goes to −∞. Neither has a minimum value (both unbounded below). The asymptote is a supremum, not a minimum.
a+b+c=f(1); vertex (9,−14) with upward opening (a>0) gives f(1)=64a−14>−14. Only −12 satisfies a>0. Evaluate the quadratic at x=1 using vertex form.
p(−1)=0 and p(2)=0 from the table, so (x+1) and (x−2) are factors; (x+1)(x−2) divides p. Read zeros from the table and apply the factor theorem.
Vertex at x=−3; one intercept at x=−17/4 is 5/4 left of axis, so the other is 5/4 right at x=−7/4. Parabola symmetry about the axis of symmetry.
Zeros at −20 and −4; vertex x-coordinate r=(−20+(−4))/2=−12. Midpoint of roots by symmetry of a parabola. Free-response.
Factored form (x+3)(x+1) has zeros at −3 and −1; vertex x=(−3+(−1))/2=−2, which lies in (−3,1). Read zeros from factored form and use symmetry.
f(0)=1+b=−25 gives b=−26; f(2)=a²−26=23 gives a=7 (a>0). So a+b=−19. Solve for constants by substituting given points into the exponential function. Free-response.
Width w, length w+5, area w(w+5)=104 → w²+5w−104=0 → (w+13)(w−8)=0 → w=8, length=13. Translate words into a quadratic and factor. Free-response.

Exponent (4/3)t rescales t so the base 1.04 period aligns with 18 months; computing the multiplier over 1.5 years extracts the percent increase n=4. Exponent time-unit conversion and percent↔factor reading.
Decreases by 80% → retains 20% → multiplier 0.20. f(1)=86×0.20=17.2, f(2)=17.2×0.20=3.44. Apply successive decay multipliers. Free-response.
Exponential with yearly growth 1.02; converting to quarters via t=q/4 gives (1.02)^(q/4). Distractors misapply the exponent rescaling direction or compound the base incorrectly.
Volume = length × width × height = x(x−7)(9) = 9x(x−7); requires translating 'length is 7 more than width' to width = x−7 and multiplying by height 9.
Zeros of g(x)=x(x−2)(x+6)^2 are 0, 2, −6; setting 7−w equal to each yields w=7, 5, 13 with sum 25.
Substituting x=c gives 80/c=10 so c=8; then p(12)=(16+160)/16=11. Each wrong answer stems from an arithmetic misstep in the two-step substitution.
Vertex form a(x−h)^2+k with a=1>0 gives minimum k=−4 at x=2. Distractors confuse the vertex coordinates or misread the sign of k.
Rewriting (1.84)^(x/4) as ((1.84)^(1/4))^x ≈ (1.165)^x gives p≈16. Distractors arise from dividing the percent linearly by 4 or dividing the base itself instead of taking the fourth root.
Constant multiplicative factor of 4 per unit x with y(0)=200 is exponential: y=200(4)^x. Distractors swap initial value and base or use a polynomial form.
A 45% decrease per unit means multiplying by 0.55 each step, giving q(x)=14(0.55)^x. Key errors: swapping base and coefficient, or using 1.45 (increase) instead of 0.55 (decrease).
Both increasing exponentials (base 1.4>1) have minimums at x=0 requiring multi-factor products to compute, so neither form displays the minimum as a single visible constant or coefficient.
Zeros are x=d (repeated from (x−d)^2), x=−d, x=−g; since d,g are unique positive constants, there are 3 distinct x-intercepts. Counting all four factors as distinct gives the trap answer 4.
Vertex x = average of zeros (10+(−13))/2 = −3/2. Distractors include y-intercept f(0)=−130, one zero (−13), or the average of misread signs (−23/2).
Setting area = (1/2)(2x+22)(x−10) = x^2 and expanding yields 2x−220=0, so x=110.
From graph points f(x)=6/(x+4); applying g(x)=f(x+4)=6/((x+4)+4)=6/(x+8). Distractors misapply the horizontal shift or return f(x) itself.
Exponents 1,5,9 at x=1,2,3 have constant difference 4, giving f(x)=a^(4x−3); solving 4k−3=29 yields k=8.
The positive x-intercept of a height-vs-time quadratic is where h=0, meaning the projectile hits the ground. Distractors confuse it with the initial height, max height, or time of max height.
Only f(x)=128(2)^(x−1) gives f(1)=128·2^0=128, where 128 appears as the coefficient. All other forms yield f(1) values not visible in the equation.
3% annual growth gives P=50000(1.03)^t; setting equal to 60000 yields 60000=50000(1.03)^t. Distractors confuse 0.03 (rate) with 1.03 (multiplier) or swap initial and target values.
Years to months via t=m/12 gives 90000(1.06)^(m/12). Distractors incorrectly divide the initial value or the base by 12 instead of rescaling the exponent.
A 190% increase means multiplying by 1+1.90=2.90, giving C=40(2.9)^t. Distractors misinterpret the percent as 19% (A), use 1.9 without adding 1 (B), or use 19 (C).
